item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate A closely follows the frozen contract with a small, pattern-reusing implementation; Candidate B explicitly violates several required API, routing, and scope constraints.","reasons":["A preserves Add unchanged and adds the exact required Upload signature with opts ...FilesOption.","A uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", then delegates to Add, preserving existing option, request, decoding, and error semantics.","B changes Upload to accept ...FilesUploadOption, bypasses Add with a duplicate Raw.Do request path, and adds association fields—all directly contrary to the contract.","B also changes Files option interfaces and unrelated raw retry/body-ownership behavior, despite explicit instructions not to alter FilesOption behavior or refactor retry machinery."],"risks_a":["The added tests do not cover empty-name/nil-content validation or source-reader failures as required.","The retry test counts attempts but does not verify that the multipart content is intact on the retried request.","The combined validation error is less specific than separate filename and content errors."],"risks_b":["Its public Upload signature is incompatible with the exact required API.","Its duplicate upload request implementation can drift from Add semantics.","The new association-option machinery is expressly out of scope and increases public API surface substantially before need is established or specified."]}
